Create a 16:9, 7-slide data analysis report PPT targeted at technology executives and network infrastructure leaders.

The presentation should open with a title slide for the Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review, then move into global traffic growth trends -- highlighting the 17% year-over-year increase and Starlink's remarkable 3.3x surge. The third slide should rank the top 10 most popular Internet services and note the rise of generative AI. Next, cover technology adoption shifts including post-quantum encryption's dramatic jump from 2% to 13% of TLS 1.3 traffic, HTTP/3 reaching 21% adoption, and Go becoming the top API client language. The fifth slide should break down the 225 major Internet disruptions by cause, emphasizing government-directed shutdowns as the leading factor. Follow with a security-focused slide covering the 6.5% traffic mitigation rate, most-attacked sectors, Log4j persistence, and email threat metrics. Use images from the `./assets/` folder referenced in the brief. Apply a professional, data-driven visual style with a dark or navy color scheme consistent with the Cloudflare Radar aesthetic. Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.
Only the correctly saved final file is needed.

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

8	
9	## Internet Traffic Growth and Popular Services
10	
11	Global Internet traffic grew by 17% in 2024, continuing the upward trend driven by increasing reliance on the Internet for communication, commerce, entertainment, and transportation. The trend line starts mid-January to normalize for post-holiday activity.
12	
13	Google maintained its position as the most popular Internet service overall, topping the rankings for the second consecutive year. 14	
15	| Rank | Service   |
16	|------|-----------|

20	| #4   | TikTok    |

29

31	
32	![Normalized Starlink traffic worldwide showing 3.3x growth in 2024](./assets/starlink-traffic-growth-2024.jpg)
33	
34	## Technology Adoption and Usage Patterns
35	
36	Several key adoption metrics emerged from the 2024 data:
37	
38	- **Mobile OS**: 33% of traffic came from iOS devices. Apple iOS and Google Android remain the dominant mobile operating systems, with peak Android traffic share exceeding 95% in some regions and peak iOS reaching around 66%.
39	- **HTTP/3**: 21% of traffic uses HTTP/3, the most recent version of the protocol that runs on top of QUIC, providing faster connections, packet-loss mitigation, and encryption by default.
40	- **Search Engines**: Google dominates with 89% of search engine referral traffic, followed by Yandex (3.1%), Baidu (2.7%), Bing (2.6%), DuckDuckGo (0.95%), and other engines (2.2%).
41	- **Browsers**: Chrome remains the most popular browser globally.
42	- **API Client Languages**: Go is the most popular API client language with approximately 12% of automated API requests, followed by Node.js, Python (9.6%), Java (7.4%), and .NET (3.6%).
43	
44	Post-quantum encryption saw a dramatic surge in adoption during 2024. Starting at around 2% of TLS 1.3 traffic in early 2024, adoption jumped sharply following Google Chrome 124 enabling post-quantum key agreement by default on April 17, rapidly climbing to approximately 12-13%. Mozilla Firefox has also started rolling out post-quantum by default, and Apple Safari began initial testing.
45	
46	![Post-quantum encrypted traffic worldwide showing rapid adoption after Chrome 124 release](./assets/post-quantum-encryption-adoption.jpg)
47	
48	## Internet Connectivity and Disruptions
49	
50	Cloudflare observed 225 major Internet disruptions globally in 2024. These outages result from a variety of causes, and the Cloudflare Radar Outage Center tracks their scope and duration using Cloudflare traffic data.
51	
52	The leading causes of Internet disruptions were:
53	
54	| Cause                | Count |
55	|----------------------|-------|
56	| Government Directed  | 116+  |
57	| Cable Cut            | 41    |
58	| Unknown              | 16    |
59	| Power Outage         | 16    |
60	| Technical Problem    | 9     |
61	| Military Action      | 9     |
62	| Weather              | 8     |
63	| Maintenance          | 4     |
64	| Cyber Attack         | 4     |
65	| Natural Disaster     | 1     |
66	| Fire                 | 1     |
67	
68	![Causes of major Internet disruptions observed in 2024](./assets/internet-disruption-causes.jpg)
69	
70	IPv6 adoption reached 28% of dual-stack traffic during 2024. Spain recorded the highest download speed among all countries measured.
71	
72	41% of global traffic came from mobile devices, reflecting the continued importance of mobile connectivity worldwide.
73	
74	## Security Landscape
75	
76	Cloudflare mitigated 6.5% of all traffic it processed, indicating the scale of ongoing threats. The Gambling and Games sector was the most attacked industry category. Notably, 68% of global bot traffic originated from just the top 10 countries.
77	
78	The Log4j vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228), first disclosed in December 2021, continues to be actively targeted by attackers more than two years later, underscoring the persistent nature of widely known vulnerabilities.
79	
80	RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure) valid routes increased by 6.4%, an important step toward improved Internet routing security.
81	
82	## Email Security Threats
83	
84	Cloudflare's email security analysis revealed that 4.3% of emails processed were malicious. Among those malicious emails, 43% contained a deceptive link designed to trick recipients. The top-level domain .bar originated the largest share of malicious and spam email observed during the year.

91	- Security threats remained pervasive: 6.5% of all traffic was mitigated, Gambling/Games was the most targeted sector, and Log4j exploitation persists years after disclosure.

# Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review

## Source

URL: https://radar.cloudflare.com/year-in-review/2024

The Cloudflare Radar 2024 Year in Review provides a comprehensive view of Internet patterns and trends observed through Cloudflare's global network during 2024. The report covers traffic growth, popular services, technology adoption, connectivity disruptions, security threats, and email security trends. Data is derived from Cloudflare's position as a provider protecting and accelerating websites and applications for millions of customers worldwide.

## Internet Traffic Growth and Popular Services

Global Internet traffic grew by 17% in 2024, continuing the upward trend driven by increasing reliance on the Internet for communication, commerce, entertainment, and transportation. The trend line starts mid-January to normalize for post-holiday activity.

Google maintained its position as the most popular Internet service overall, topping the rankings for the second consecutive year. Generative AI continued its rapid rise throughout 2024, while the Metaverse receded into the background. The ranking methodology is based on aggregate data from Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 DNS resolver.

| Rank | Service   |

ACCENT_ORG  = RGBColor(0xF6, 0x82, 0x12)   # Cloudflare orange
ACCENT_BLUE = RGBColor(0x36, 0xA2, 0xEB)   # chart blue
ACCENT_TEAL = RGBColor(0x00, 0xC8, 0xC8)   # highlight teal

    if fill_color:

    else:

    if line_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line_color
    else:

    return shape

                font_size=Pt(14), bold=False, color=WHITE,

def fill_slide_bg(slide, color):
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_rect(slide, l, t, w, h, fill_color=None, line_color=None, line_width=Pt(0)):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(1, l, t, w, h)   # MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE = 1
    shape.line.width = line_width
    if fill_color:
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    else:
        shape.fill.background()
    if line_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line_color
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

def add_textbox(slide, text, l, t, w, h,
                font_size=Pt(14), bold=False, color=WHITE,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, word_wrap=True, italic=False):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(l, t, w, h)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = word_wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size  = font_size
    run.font.bold  = bold
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    run.font.italic = italic
    return txBox

    run.font.bold  = bold

def fill_slide_bg(slide, color):
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_rect(slide, l, t, w, h, fill_color=None, line_color=None, line_width=Pt(0)):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(1, l, t, w, h)   # MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE = 1
    shape.line.width = line_width
    if fill_color:
        shape.fill.solid()
        shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    else:
        shape.fill.background()
    if line_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line_color
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

def add_textbox(slide, text, l, t, w, h,
                font_size=Pt(14), bold=False, color=WHITE,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, word_wrap=True, italic=False):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(l, t, w, h)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = word_wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size  = font_size
    run.font.bold  = bold
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    run.font.italic = italic
    return txBox

def add_para(tf, text, font_size=Pt(13), bold=False, color=WHITE,
             align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, space_before=Pt(4), italic=False):
    p = tf.add_paragraph()
    p.alignment = align
    p.space_before = space_before
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size  = font_size
    run.font.bold  = bold
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    run.font.italic = italic
    return p

# SLIDE 6 – Security
# ==============================================================================

def slide_06(prs):
    layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    sl = prs.slides.add_slide(layout)
    fill_slide_bg(sl, NAVY)
    add_header_bar(sl, "6.5% of Traffic Mitigated: Persistent Threats and Bot Concentration",
                   "Security Findings  |  Cloudflare Network  |  2024")

    top_metrics = [
        (RED_ALERT,  "6.5%",  "Traffic\nMitigated"),
        (ACCENT_ORG, "4.3%",  "Emails\nMalicious"),
        (ACCENT_BLUE,"43%",   "Malicious Emails\nw/ Deceptive Link"),
        (GREEN,      "68%",   "Bot Traffic from\nTop 10 Countries"),
        (ACCENT_TEAL,"6.4%",  "RPKI Valid\nRoute Increase"),
    ]

    box_w = Inches(2.35)
    for i, (color, val, label) in enumerate(top_metrics):
        x = Inches(0.3 + i * 2.6)
        add_rect(sl, x, Inches(1.1), box_w, Inches(1.6),
                 fill_color=DARK_PANEL, line_color=color, line_width=Pt(2))
        add_rect(sl, x, Inches(1.1), box_w, Inches(0.07), fill_color=color)
        add_textbox(sl, val, x, Inches(1.2), box_w, Inches(0.85),
                    font_size=Pt(34), bold=True, color=color, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)
        add_textbox(sl, label, x, Inches(2.0), box_w, Inches(0.65),
                    font_size=Pt(10.5), color=LIGHT_GREY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

    # ── Three content panels ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
    panels = [
        {
            "title": "Most Attacked Sectors",
            "color": RED_ALERT,
            "items": [
                "1st  Gambling & Games — most targeted industry",
                "Bot and DDoS attacks dominate attack vectors",
                "68% of global bot traffic from just top 10 countries",
                "Automated attack tooling increasingly accessible",
            ]
        },
        {
            "title": "Log4j Persistence (CVE-2021-44228)",
            "color": ACCENT_ORG,
            "items": [
                "First disclosed December 2021 — still actively exploited",
                "Highlights danger of unpatched legacy vulnerabilities",
                "Attackers maintain persistent targeting 3+ years later",
                "RPKI valid routes +6.4% (routing security improvement)",
            ]
        },
        {
            "title": "Email Threat Metrics",
            "color": ACCENT_BLUE,
            "items": [
                "4.3% of all emails processed were malicious",
                "43% of malicious emails contained deceptive links",
                ".bar TLD originated most malicious & spam email",
                "Phishing via link deception remains dominant vector",
            ]
        },
    ]

    for i, panel in enumerate(panels):
        x = Inches(0.3 + i * 4.35)
        color = panel["color"]
        add_rect(sl, x, Inches(2.85), Inches(4.1), Inches(3.75),

        add_rect(sl, x, Inches(2.85), Inches(4.1), Inches(0.42), fill_color=color)
        add_textbox(sl, panel["title"], x + Inches(0.1), Inches(2.88),
                    Inches(3.9), Inches(0.38), font_size=Pt(12), bold=True, color=NAVY)
        for j, item in enumerate(panel["items"]):
            add_textbox(sl, f"• {item}",
                        x + Inches(0.12), Inches(3.38 + j * 0.74),
                        Inches(3.9), Inches(0.68),
                        font_size=Pt(10.5), color=LIGHT_GREY)

    add_rect(sl, Inches(0), Inches(6.9), SLIDE_W, Inches(0.6), fill_color=DARK_PANEL)
    add_textbox(sl, "Source: Cloudflare Radar  |  radar.cloudflare.com/year-in-review/2024",
                Inches(0.3), Inches(6.95), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
                font_size=Pt(10), color=MID_GREY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# ==============================================================================
# SLIDE 7 – Takeaways
# ==============================================================================

def slide_07(prs):
    layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]
    sl = prs.slides.add_slide(layout)
    fill_slide_bg(sl, NAVY)
    add_header_bar(sl, "Five Takeaways Shaping the 2025 Internet Outlook",
                   "Strategic Implications for Network and Security Leaders")

    takeaways = [
        {
            "num": "01",
            "title": "Internet Traffic Growth Trajectory",
            "body": (
                "Global traffic grew 17% YoY; Starlink's 3.3x surge signals satellite connectivity"
                " entering the mainstream. Capacity planning must account for accelerating demand"
                " from underserved regions."
            ),
            "color": ACCENT_BLUE,
        },
        {
            "num": "02",
            "title": "Post-Quantum Encryption Momentum",
            "body": (
                "Adoption leapt from 2% to 13% of TLS 1.3 traffic following Chrome 124's default"
                " enablement. Organizations should evaluate post-quantum readiness before broader"
                " browser and OS rollouts accelerate the curve further."
            ),
            "color": ACCENT_TEAL,
        },
        {
            "num": "03",
            "title": "Connectivity Fragility from Government Actions",
            "body": (
                "Government-directed shutdowns caused 116+ of 225 major disruptions — more than"
                " all technical causes combined. Resilience strategies must factor in geopolitical"
                " risk alongside infrastructure failure."
            ),
            "color": RED_ALERT,
        },
        {
            "num": "04",
            "title": "Persistent Security Threats at Scale",
            "body": (
                "6.5% of all traffic required mitigation; Log4j exploitation continues 3+ years"
                " after disclosure. Patch velocity and threat-intelligence sharing remain critical"
                " — legacy vulnerabilities do not self-remediate."
            ),
            "color": ACCENT_ORG,
        },
        {
            "num": "05",
            "title": "Evolving Developer & Protocol Ecosystem",
            "body": (
                "Go leads API client languages (~12%); HTTP/3 reached 21% adoption. The shift"
                " to modern protocols and languages reflects a developer ecosystem optimizing"
                " for performance, concurrency, and encrypted-by-default connectivity."
            ),
            "color": GREEN,
        },
    ]

    col_positions = [Inches(0.3), Inches(6.9)]
    row_positions  = [Inches(1.12), Inches(3.1), Inches(5.08)]

    layout_order = [
        (0, 0), (0, 1),   # row 0: items 0, 1
        (1, 0), (1, 1),   # row 1: items 2, 3
        (2, 0),            # row 2: item 4 (spans both cols)
    ]

    card_w_single = Inches(6.2)
    card_w_full   = Inches(12.8)
    card_h        = Inches(1.82)

    for idx, (row, col) in enumerate(layout_order):
        tw = takeaways[idx]
        x = col_positions[col]
        y = row_positions[row]
        w = card_w_full if (row == 2) else card_w_single
        color = tw["color"]

        add_rect(sl, x, y, w, card_h,
                 fill_color=DARK_PANEL, line_color=color, line_width=Pt(1.5))
        add_rect(sl, x, y, Inches(0.08), card_h, fill_color=color)

        # Number badge
        add_rect(sl, x + Inches(0.15), y + Inches(0.15),
                 Inches(0.55), Inches(0.55), fill_color=color)
        add_textbox(sl, tw["num"],
                    x + Inches(0.15), y + Inches(0.15),
                    Inches(0.55), Inches(0.55),
                    font_size=Pt(14), bold=True, color=NAVY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

        title_x = x + Inches(0.82)
        title_w = w - Inches(1.0)
        add_textbox(sl, tw["title"],
                    title_x, y + Inches(0.14), title_w, Inches(0.45),
                    font_size=Pt(13), bold=True, color=color)
        add_textbox(sl, tw["body"],
                    title_x, y + Inches(0.56), title_w, Inches(1.18),
                    font_size=Pt(10.5), color=LIGHT_GREY)

    add_rect(sl, Inches(0), Inches(6.9), SLIDE_W, Inches(0.6), fill_color=DARK_PANEL)
    add_textbox(sl, "Source: Cloudflare Radar  |  radar.cloudflare.com/year-in-review/2024",
                Inches(0.3), Inches(6.95), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
                font_size=Pt(10), color=MID_GREY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# ==============================================================================
# Main
# ==============================================================================

def main():
    prs = new_prs()
    slide_01(prs)
    slide_02(prs)
    slide_03(prs)
    slide_04(prs)
    slide_05(prs)
    slide_06(prs)
    slide_07(prs)

    out_path = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(out_path), exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(out_path)
    print(f"Saved: {out_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
